title: Toyota Corolla
wiki_lead:
The Toyota Corolla (Japanese: トヨタ・カローラ, Hepburn: Toyota Karōra) is a series of compact cars (formerly subcompact) manufactured and marketed globally by the Japanese automaker Toyota Motor Corporation since 1966. Since 1997, the Corolla has remained the best-selling automobile nameplate of all time, surpassing the Volkswagen Beetle. Toyota reached the milestone of 50 million Corollas sold over twelve generations in 2021, and has sold over 54 million units as of early 2026.
The name Corolla is part of Toyota's naming tradition of using names derived from the Toyota Crown for sedans, with "corolla" meaning "small crown" in Latin. The Corolla has always been exclusive in Japan to Toyota Corolla Store locations, and manufactured in Japan with a twin, called the Toyota Sprinter until 2000. From 2006 to 2018 in Japan and much of the world, and from 2018 to 2020 in Taiwan, the hatchback companion had been called the Toyota Auris.
Early models were mostly rear-wheel drive, while later models have been front-wheel drive. Four-wheel drive versions have also been produced, and it has undergone several major redesigns. The Corolla's traditional competitors have been the Nissan Sunny, introduced the same year as the Corolla in Japan and the later Subaru Leone, Honda Civic, and Mitsubishi Lancer. The Corolla's chassis designation code is "E", as described in Toyota's chassis and engine codes.

Production locations

Corollas are manufactured in Japan at the original Takaoka plant built in 1966. Various production facilities have been built in Brazil, (Indaiatuba, São Paulo), Canada (Cambridge, Ontario), China (Tianjin), Pakistan (Karachi), South Africa (Durban), Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam, Turkey (Sakarya), and the United Kingdom (Derbyshire). Production or assembly has previously been carried out in Australia (Dandenong and Altona), India (Bangalore), Indonesia (Jakarta), Malaysia (Shah Alam), New Zealand (Thames), the Philippines (Santa Rosa, Laguna), and Venezuela.
Corollas were made at NUMMI in Fremont, California until March 2010. Production resumed in November 2011 at Toyota Motor Manufacturing Mississippi in Blue Springs, Mississippi.


First generation (E10; 1966)

The first generation Corolla was unveiled at the 1966 Tokyo Motor Show and then introduced in November in the same year with the new 1100 cc K pushrod engine. The Corolla Sprinter was introduced as the fastback version in 1968, and exclusive to a Toyota Japan dealership retail outlet called Toyota Auto Store. It was the second car available to Japanese buyers at Toyota Corolla Store next to the smaller Publica.


Second generation (E20; 1970)

In May 1970, the E20 was restyled with a more rounded body. The now mutually exclusive Corolla and Sprinter names were used to differentiate between two slightly different treatments of sheet metal and trim. grok_lead: The Toyota Corolla is a line of subcompact and compact cars manufactured by Toyota Motor Corporation, first introduced in November 1966 as a 1-liter-class, five-seat sedan positioned between the smaller Publica and larger Corona models. It quickly became a symbol of reliable, economical transportation, evolving through 12 generations to encompass various body styles including sedans, hatchbacks, wagons, and crossovers, while emphasizing fuel efficiency, safety, and global adaptability. The Corolla has a reputation for exceptional longevity and durability, with many vehicles routinely exceeding 200,000â300,000 miles with proper maintenance, and documented cases existing of vehicles surpassing 400,000â500,000 miles. Reliability ratings vary by generation and source; recent models from the 2020s often receive predicted reliability scores of 4/5 or 5/5 from Consumer Reports, while earlier generations such as the tenth (2006â2013) have received average ratings from the same source. iSeeCars studies indicate that Toyota vehicles, including the Corolla, have a higher-than-average probability of reaching high mileage compared to the industry norm. Despite this strong reputation for reliability, some common owner-reported issues include check engine lights caused by problems in the evaporative emissions (EVAP) system, often related to the gas cap or charcoal canister, as well as, in some recent models such as the 2019 Corolla, orange (amber) dashboard warning lights that indicate cautions, malfunctions, or items needing attention but not immediate danger (unlike red lights which signal urgent issues). Common orange lights include the master warning light (triangle with exclamation mark) for general system issues often accompanied by a message or buzzer, the tire pressure warning light (U-shaped tire with exclamation) for low tire pressure or TPMS malfunction, the malfunction indicator lamp/check engine light (engine outline) for issues in the engine, emissions, or related systems, the slip indicator (car with wavy lines) for traction control/VSC issues or operation, the low fuel level warning for low fuel requiring refueling soon, and the LDA (Lane Departure Alert) indicator signaling malfunction or operation of the lane assist system. Drivers should consult the multi-information display for accompanying messages and refer to the owner's manual for precise meanings; if a light remains on, have the vehicle inspected by a Toyota dealer. In addition, some recent models experience transmission vibrations or weak 12-volt batteries in hybrid variants. According to RepairPal, the average annual repair and maintenance cost for a Toyota Corolla is $362, slightly higher than the Mazda CX-3's $345. Both models are rated as having excellent ownership costs, with low severity and average to low frequency of repairs. By 2021, the Corolla had achieved the historic milestone of 50 million units sold worldwide, making it the best-selling automobile nameplate in history and a cornerstone of Toyota's success in leading Japan's motorization wave and international markets. Spanning over five decades, the Corolla's generations reflect Toyota's commitment to innovation and responsiveness to market demands. The first generation (1966â1970) established its foundational design as an affordable, durable vehicle that propelled Toyota's export growth. Subsequent generations introduced key advancements: the second (1970â1974) added the sporty Corolla Sprinter coupe; the third (1974â1979) expanded dimensions for improved safety and emissions compliance; the fourth (1979â1983) offered seven body variations; and the fifth (1983â1987) transitioned sedans to front-wheel drive while retaining rear-wheel drive for coupes. Later iterations, such as the sixth (1987â1991) and seventh (1991â1995), targeted a premium global sedan image with enhanced size and features, while the eighth (1995â2000) prioritized environmental and safety improvements, including lighter construction and new high-performance engines like the 165 PS 1.6-liter unit. The ninth through eleventh generations (2000â2016) streamlined offerings to sedans and wagons, discontinued some sports variants, and integrated advanced technologies such as rearview monitors and compact efficiency designs, culminating in the twelfth generation (introduced in 2018 and ongoing). This current lineup, now in its mature phase as of 2026, includes gasoline, hybrid, and performance-oriented models like the GR Corolla. Gasoline models have EPA-estimated fuel economy of up to 32 mpg city/41 mpg highway/35 mpg combined for the 2025 Toyota Corolla LE (gasoline, base trim with 2.0-liter Dynamic Force 4-cylinder engine producing 169 hp at 6600 rpm and 151 lb-ft of torque); the navigation package or its absence does not impact these ratings, as they are based on the powertrain and standard configuration. Other trims have similar figures such as 31 mpg city/40 mpg highway/34 mpg combined. Hybrid models feature the fifth-generation Toyota Hybrid System and achieve up to 53 mpg city/46 mpg highway/50 mpg combined (FWD LE trim). The 2026 model year retains these ratings with no significant changes to powertrain or efficiency reported. In China, the 2026 Toyota Corolla (including related Levin variants) received a facelift featuring a redesigned front end adopting Toyota's "Hammerhead" design language, with C-shaped LED headlights connected by a thin illuminated strip, low-mounted high and low beams at the outer bumper edges, a dark horizontal grille, and a more prominent front spoiler. This front design draws inspiration from the latest Prius and RAV4 models. Recent additions, such as the 2025 Corolla FX trim with its sporty blacked-out styling and the versatile Corolla Cross crossover, continue to blend modern aesthetics, Toyota Safety Sense 3.0 advanced driver-assistance systems, and electrified powertrains across sedan, hatchback, and hybrid variants, along with interior lighting upgrades. The 2024 Toyota Corolla dome light uses a DE3175 (31mm festoon) bulb, which is typically incandescent from the factory, with LED-compatible replacements in DE3175 size widely available and commonly installed as upgrades for brighter, more efficient interior lighting without issues. Produced in multiple countries including the United States since the mid-1980s, the Corolla remains a benchmark for dependability, having earned accolades like the 2007 Good Design Award for its tenth-generation Axio model and sustaining its position as a top global seller.
